summary: Coup is a fast, cutthroat bluffing game where players claim character powers they may or may not actually hold, daring others to challenge them. It's tense and social, with the whole game riding on reading opponents' nerve and managing your dwindling influence cards.
praised: great for groups who enjoy social deduction
high replayability despite tiny card count
criticised: player elimination can leave people waiting out a round
some feel it's more about table read than skill

interaction.kind: direct attacks (coups, assassinations, stealing coins) and bluffing accusations aimed at specific opponents
interaction.detail: Nearly every action either takes coins directly from a targeted player, forces them to lose an influence card, or challenges their bluff, and the game ends by eliminating opponents one by one. There is no personal board at all — the only shared state is the pool of coins and each player's dwindling influence, all of which are fought over directly.
interaction.said: "cutthroat", "bluffing and backstabbing", "screw your neighbor", "brutal" — Coup is consistently described as a mean, direct, elimination-driven game

scoring.how_you_win: There is no point total — players bluff character powers and challenge or block opponents to strip away their hidden influence cards, and the last player left with any influence remaining wins.
